ai_boundary: AI_PROPOSED is reserved in the ClassificationMethod enum for a future round; R5 never produces it and makes no LLM/provider call.
ambiguity_policy: AMBIGUOUS requires at least two distinct candidates and never auto-selects a winner.
approval_distinction: ClassificationRecord carries no approved/approval_status/authoritative_truth field. CLASSIFIED is a resolution state, not a Technical Lead approval (R9).
batch_policy: classify_batch evaluates each request independently and preserves original input order in both accepted and rejected lists.
candidate_policy: candidate_natures is canonicalized to a duplicate-free tuple sorted by enum value before storage; unknown/invalid enum values are rejected, never coerced.
canonical_knowledge_distinction: Classification never creates a KnowledgeStatement or any canonical Knowledge Source content (R10).
classification_record_contract: ClassificationRecord{classification_id, material_id, source_type, status, classification_method, selected_nature?, candidate_natures[], rationale?, classified_by?, metadata}. CLASSIFIED requires exactly one selected_nature and no candidates; UNCLASSIFIED requires neither; AMBIGUOUS requires no selected_nature and >=2 distinct candidates.
external_io_policy: No file open, network fetch, API call, or directory scan occurs anywhere in this module. Classification operates only on an already-ingested MaterialItem and explicitly supplied enum values/text.
failure_isolation_policy: One invalid batch request is rejected with a sanitized, deterministic reason; it never removes or corrupts another request's acceptance.
identity_policy: classification_id is derived via stable_id from (material_id, status, selected_nature, canonical candidate tuple, classification_method) only — rationale/classified_by/metadata are excluded from identity as attribution/explanatory data, not decision data.

knowledge_natures.notes: May describe an existing (descriptive) or intended (prescriptive) architecture.
knowledge_natures.semantic_role: Architectural description, principle, topology, component relationship, or technical structural design.

knowledge_natures.notes: Not automatically equivalent to corporate governance NORM.
A structural listing, not a narrative process description.
knowledge_natures.semantic_role: Inventory/listing of available or existing entities, capabilities, or resources.

knowledge_natures.notes: A bounding condition, not evidence that the current system already satisfies or violates it.
knowledge_natures.semantic_role: Technical, organizational, regulatory, operational, or project constraint.

knowledge_natures.notes: Classification as DECISION does not itself establish approval authority.
knowledge_natures.semantic_role: Explicit choice among alternatives or direction selected by an authorized process/person.

knowledge_natures.notes: Classification alone does not prove the implementation currently exists; evidence/provenance is still required by later knowledge stages.
knowledge_natures.semantic_role: Description of what is currently implemented.

knowledge_natures.notes: May be narrower than a PROCESS; R5 does not attempt semantic decomposition.
Reflective/retrospective in nature, not a mandatory rule by itself.
knowledge_natures.semantic_role: Recorded lesson learned or experience-derived guidance.

knowledge_natures.notes: Describes what has been observed/documented, not what must be.
knowledge_natures.semantic_role: Descriptive inventory or documented observation of the current state (current tool inventory, current agent inventory, system survey, technical/functional survey).

knowledge_natures.notes: Precedes REQUIREMENT in maturity; not itself a formal commitment.
knowledge_natures.semantic_role: Need, problem, or objective that motivates work but may not yet be a formal requirement.

knowledge_natures.notes: Does not imply implementation or compliance.
knowledge_natures.semantic_role: Prescriptive rule defining how something should be done (governance rule, development standard, security rule, methodology, mandatory operating rule).

knowledge_natures.notes: May be broader than a single FLOW; R5 does not decompose one into the other.
Scope is the project itself, not a specific rule/process/architecture within it.
knowledge_natures.semantic_role: Knowledge describing a project, accompaniment, initiative, or project-specific context.

knowledge_natures.notes: Do not assume REQUIREMENT implies TO_BE unless temporal state was explicitly established elsewhere.
knowledge_natures.semantic_role: Explicit requirement stating something that must be satisfied.

knowledge_natures.notes: Kept distinct from generic DECISION only when the caller explicitly distinguishes them.
knowledge_natures.semantic_role: Formal resolution/outcome addressing a previously identified matter.

knowledge_natures.notes: Instructional content aimed at people, not a system specification.

material_linkage: By material_id only (legacy_documenter.knowledge.domain.models.MaterialItem.material_id); no material payload is duplicated inside a ClassificationRecord.
note: SOURCE_TYPE_IS_NOT_KNOWLEDGE_NATURE. CLASSIFIED_IS_NOT_APPROVED_KNOWLEDGE. Classification records what semantic nature has been explicitly established for already-ingested material; it never establishes truth, currency, approval, or canonical status.
provenance_distinction: Classification never creates, rewrites, or reads R3 ProvenanceGraph state; the two concerns are independent and both keyed by material_id only.
security_policy: rationale, classified_by, and metadata are sanitized (reusing the existing sanitizer and R2's metadata validator) before storage.
serialization_policy: candidate_natures is always stored pre-sorted; two ClassificationRecords built from the same candidate set in different input orders are structurally identical and serialize byte-identically.
source_type_distinction: source_type is copied from the classified MaterialItem and never mutated. It is preserved for correlation only, never used to derive selected_nature.
temporal_distinction: Classification never reads or infers MaterialItem.temporal_state; the same selected_nature is valid regardless of AS_IS/TO_BE/HISTORICAL/None.
unclassified_policy: UNCLASSIFIED requires no selected_nature and no candidates; it is a legitimate, permanent-until-revisited lifecycle state, not an error or a default fallback.
